sessions.goal: Play the first 10 minutes as a brand-new player who has never seen the game; note every moment of confusion.
sessions.verdict: The opening loop (tips, top-left objective, chop trees, then N, F and E) is clear, and its feedback is good: floating +wood text, rewards, a helpful 'too close' message. But two of the first six objectives complete without the player doing them ('Eat something' and 'Build a market stall', the stall built by an NPC), so the tutorial teaches less than it seems to. Founding a settlement is the big stall point: the crowded world plus compass directions with no compass on screen cause several minutes of wandering. Several HUD text overflows and overlaps make the screen look unfinished at 960x540.

sessions.goal: Reach the Village era as fast as you can (it cannot come before day 3, about 17 minutes of game time); record the game time of every objective.
sessions.verdict: The early loop moves fast and is well signposted. Six objectives were done in 143 game seconds, and the 'too close to X, open ground lies N to the south' hints made placing a settlement easy. Once the settlement exists, NPCs build stalls and buildings for you, and the only things left are a fixed day-3 timer and recruiting members, so the Village era turns into waiting. The two different meanings of 'Village' on screen make that wait confusing. On this loaded machine (about 12 tps) the day-3 gate could not be reached in the session at all.

sessions.goal: Survive the first winter. Start with `--season autumn` (a fresh world otherwise reaches winter only after about 57 minutes of game time). Note how food and cold feel.
sessions.verdict: Early autumn plays smoothly: wood, a nation, a settlement and a farm in about 10,000 ticks, with useful refusal messages and a lively chronicle of rival nations. But --season autumn leaves winter two game days away, so neither winter nor the cold could be tested in a 35-minute session. Food creates no pressure in autumn: apples pile up from chopping and energy never fell below 84. Low fps also makes the two-click confirms and the reflowing action bar easy to misclick.

sessions.goal: Diplomacy and war: lead a nation, meet a neighbour, try alliance, rivalry and war from the Nations screen (O).
sessions.verdict: The Nations screen is clear and responsive: every action gives a precise status line with the relation number and threshold, Peace and Confirm buttons appear only when they apply, and the chronicle records each step. But because the screen pauses the world, the whole cycle (alliance for 75 coins, rivalry, war, instant peace, war again through a truce) costs no game time and almost nothing else, so diplomacy feels like flipping switches rather than statecraft. The short real-time window for click-again confirmations is also hard to hit at low frame rates.

sessions.goal: Trade and caravans: build a market stall, buy and sell, get a Storehouse and send a caravan.
sessions.verdict: The early loop (chop, nation, found) flows well, and the error messages are good: they give spacing hints with distance and direction, and say why a merchant can't pay. But the trade goal falls apart. NPCs fill the player's own market before the player can build a stall, and the stall objective completes from their stall. Selling is starved of coins. The Storehouse and caravans sit behind the Town era, at least 3 game days away. The build-confirm window also times out at low tps (the machine was at load ~54, 2 fps / 7-15 tps; the first pt start timed out).

sessions.goal: Ruler, laws and heirs: lead a nation, enact and repeal laws, and see what happens when the ruler dies.
sessions.verdict: Founding a nation and passing or repealing laws works, and the chronicle reports each change clearly ('Taxes in Redfield rose to High', 'Redfield stood down its conscripts'). But laws do nothing you can see in a one-member nation. Pawns are hard to recruit, and the AI nations sign them all up within minutes. Succession has no presence in the UI at all, so the ruler-and-heirs part of this goal could not be reached or even planned for in normal play.

sessions.goal: Crafting: find and use every recipe on the crafting screen (C); are tools worth making?
sessions.verdict: Tools are worth making and the screen explains them well. An axe (4 wood, 2 stone) pays for itself after two trees and gives about +60 wood over 20 uses; the pickaxe gives +30 stone over 15 uses. The live 'Ready / Need N more / have 1 (19 uses left)' lines and the context 'Craft Pickaxe' HUD button are good. Cooked Meat is the weak recipe: you can't choose to eat it, and auto-eat spends it first at 89 energy, so most of its 45 energy is thrown away. Planks and Bricks can't be reached in a first session (Village era: 10 members, 2 stalls, day 3), so only 3 of the 5 recipes could be used.

sessions.goal: World events: play until world events are offered, take different choices, and judge whether the consequences are clear and fair.
sessions.verdict: The world-event sheet works well. The Drought sheet names the cause, gives each option's cost and effect, pauses the world, and the result line is clear. A save reload replays the same event, so all three choices could be compared. The weak spots are around it. Ration's 'restless' penalty is hidden. Irrigation silently draws on stores. Nation world events are lost in raid spam in a chronicle labelled 'your news'. The first player event comes about 10 game minutes in, so only one event (Drought) was seen in this session, under heavy machine load (about 3-15 tps).

sessions.goal: Accessibility and text audit, touching only what a mouse-and-keyboard player would: every screen and panel; cut-off, overlapping, unclear or misspelled text; contrast; anything only explained on hover.
sessions.verdict: Text is almost always plain-language and the in-world dark panels, crafting cards, Controls pages and error banners read well. The main accessibility problems are low contrast on the light-blue menu screens, HUD panels that move and overlap (Inventory Info jumps mid-screen and gets covered by tips), a translucent Chronicle window, and a recent-chronicle panel that truncates every line. Nothing is explained on hover anywhere, so disabled buttons and Config jargon go unexplained.

sessions.goal: Save/load and share-seed round trip: save from the pause menu, stop, `pt start --continue`, confirm the world is identical; then start a new world from the seed shown on the Share screen and confirm it matches.
sessions.verdict: Save/continue is solid: the pause-menu Save gives clear feedback ('Saved: Day 1 - no nation, 08:02'), --continue restored tick, position, heading, energy, inventory, objective and chronicle exactly, with a friendly 'Welcome back' toast, and Main Menu > Load restored the right slot. The Share screen's seed reproduces the starting map exactly, but the world's history (which nations form, their names and timing) diverges, so a shared seed is a shared map rather than a shared story; save slots also need more distinguishing detail than 'Day 1 - no nation'.

findings.title: Objective 6 'Build a market stall' completes by itself when a resident builds a stall
findings.detail: Objective needs Wood 20 / Stone 5. It completed at tick 6250 while I had Wood 2 / Stone 0 and had just exited the settlement; nothing was spent. The settlement's market later lists 'Merchants: Lily Williams' (1/4 stalls), so an NPC resident built it. No message said so, and I went on gathering wood and stone for a stall I never needed. Expected the objective to need the player's own B/Build Stall, or at least a message crediting the resident.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/bn-pt-064 --seed 101; reach objective 6 (found a settlement ~ (475,-446), press E to enter, then click Exit Settlement); wait ~200 ticks; pt events shows objective_completed build-stall with Wood still 2

Objective 6 'Build a market stall' completes when an NPC builds a stall, without the player doing anything

findings.title: Build-confirm window is ~1 game second, so a normal second click times out at low tps
findings.detail: Build Farm asks you to 'Click again to confirm'. Three separate clicks on 'Confirm Build Farm' failed with 'Not confirmed in time, so nothing was done.' and the button re-armed. Only two clicks fired 1.7 s apart in real time worked. The window looks like ~50 ticks, which is several real seconds at 9 tps but too short with 2 fps hover-then-click. It should be measured in real time (or be longer).
findings.repro: Inside own settlement with 25 wood/10 stone: pt click 473 445; pt wait 2; pt click 473 445 -> re-arms instead of building
alsoTitled: Two-click confirm on Build Farm times out in ~70 ticks, too short at low fps

findings.title: Game ran at 0.2-16 tps (normally 50) on the shared machine, so the day-3 Village gate could not be reached in a 35-minute session
findings.detail: pt status/state showed tps between 0.2 and 16, mostly 11-13, with fps 0-3 (load average about 55). Game time ran at roughly a quarter of real time. After 25 minutes of wall-clock time the game was at tick 10270, still day 1 (timeOfDay 0.64). Every other Village requirement was met or nearly met by tick 8800. At this rate day 3 (about tick 60000) would take over an hour of real time. walkto also timed out several times because it steers at 2-3 fps.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/bn-pt-064 --seed 102 with several sessions in parallel; play for 25 minutes; pt state shows tps and tick
alsoTitled: Game ran at 2-4 fps / 5-18 tps on the shared machine; first start timed out

findings.title: --season autumn starts at autumn day 1/2, so winter is still ~52k ticks (over an hour of wall time) away
findings.detail: With --season autumn the world opens at tick 120044 (day 4), and the Season panel says 'Autumn - day 1/2, Winter in 2 days'. Winter begins at tick 180000. At the 9-17 tps this machine managed, I reached tick ~130700 by the end of a 25-minute session, so winter was never reached and the cold could not be tested. Expected: a start that puts winter within a playtest's reach, such as the last day of autumn or a --season winter-eve option.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/bn-pt-064 --seed 103 --season autumn; pt key space; pt click 480 315; pt click 480 315; pt state (tick 120044, season panel 'Winter in 2 days')

findings.title: Cooked Meat is wasted by auto-eat: eaten first at <90 energy, capped at 100
findings.detail: Crafted 1 Cooked Meat (screen says '45 energy (raw: 25)'). There is no eat key or button; the player auto-eats when energy drops below 90 and always picks the most nourishing food first. The cooked meat disappeared around tick 3250-3303 (only visible cue: 'Objective complete: Eat something'), and energy went from ~90 to 99.2. So ~35 of its 45 energy was lost while the bag held 12+ apples (15 each) that would have fit exactly. Cooking a chicken (costing a wood) currently buys almost nothing. Expected: eat the smallest food that fills the gap, or let the player choose when to eat.
findings.repro: pt start --seed 107; key space; click Start/Begin; walkto tree, e; walkto chicken, e; key c; click Craft on Cooked Meat (822,265); keep gathering until energy < 90; watch the cooked_meat count drop and energy cap at 100

findings.title: Diplomacy happens with no game time passing: Nations screen pauses the world, so ally/denounce/war/peace all resolve on one tick
findings.detail: With the Nations screen open the tick stayed at 1387 (tps 0). In that frozen moment I went Neutral 0 -> three Tributes (+30, 75 of 199 coins) -> Ally accepted -> Denounce x2 (Rival -20) -> War (Hostile -60) -> Peace accepted -> War again. No cooldowns, no diminishing returns on gifts. An alliance with the first neighbour cost 75 coins and ~20 s real time. Expected gifts or relation changes to need some game time or have a cooldown.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/bn-pt-064 --seed 104; title/Start/Begin; pt key n; pt wait 60 (Westshire is founded ~tick 851); pt key o; click Tribute (123,218) x3; click Ally (301,218)

findings.title: NPCs fill all 4 market stalls in a new settlement before the player can build one; B says 'Market is full'
findings.detail: I founded a settlement at tick 5750 with 4 wood left (founding takes 50 of the 54 I had), then left to chop the 20 wood a stall needs. By tick 6802 NPCs (Dave Robinson, Mike Roberts, Lily Wood) had built all 4 stalls in MY settlement ('The market is now full'). Back inside with 22 wood/5 stone, B gave 'Market is full. Cannot build stall.' The player never gets to build a stall in their own settlement. Expected: a stall slot kept for the leader, or NPCs waiting until the player has had a chance.
findings.repro: pt start --seed 105; gather ~54 wood; N; walk to open ground; F; E (enter); Exit Settlement; chop 20 wood (~1300 ticks); walkto settlement; e; b

findings.title: Player's nation cannot realistically gain members: pawns flee after one talk and all join AI nations within minutes
findings.detail: Irene Taylor: 'I don't even know you.' (needs Acquaintance). After one E-talk pawns walk off, so the next E 1 s later says 'No entities within range'. Gifting (G, 10 coins each) to Wendy Wilson reached Acquaintance after 3 gifts, but by then she and Hank Davies were sworn to Smalltown ('I'm loyal to Smalltown.' (needs Loyal)). By day 1 morning 9 AI nations existed (Smalltown, Newwood, Towntown, Upperburg, Littleburg, Whiteland, Northernland, Townfield, Easternham), leaving Redfield at 1 member for the whole session. With 1 member, taxes collect 0 coins and conscription ('one conscript per 2 members') yields nothing, so the laws had no observable effect and no heir could exist.
findings.repro: seed 106; key n; walkto pawn; key e; key r -> needs Acquaintance; walkto pawn (Smalltown villager); key g x3; key r -> needs Loyal

findings.title: Ruler death / succession cannot be reached or even learned about in normal play within a session
findings.detail: The goal's third part (what happens when the ruler dies) was not reachable. Nothing on screen (Nations tab 'You lead it', Laws tab, Player Info 'Role: LEADER', all 3 pages of ? Controls) mentions an heir, succession, or ruler death. The only way to die seems to be energy reaching 0: energy drained ~85 -> 57.6 over 8210 ticks (~164 game s), i.e. ~6 more game minutes, which at the observed 7-16 tps is 25+ real minutes. And with no other nation members there would be no heir anyway. Expected: the Nations tab to name the current heir (or say 'no heir: Redfield ends with you') so a player can plan a dynasty.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/bn-pt-064 --seed 106; space; click Start; click Begin; key n; key o; read both tabs; open ? Controls pages 1-3

findings.title: War/Denounce click-again confirmation expires in a few seconds of real time; at 2-5 fps the second click often misses it
findings.detail: Clicking War relabels the button 'Confirm' and arms a confirmation, which expires with 'Not confirmed in time, so nothing was done.' after roughly 4-9 s of real time (it varied, suggesting it may be frame-dependent). With hover-before-click at a few fps, a normal second click arrived after expiry and just re-armed it. It took 5 attempts (~2.5 min) until two back-to-back clicks worked. Expected the confirmation to last longer, or to be a modal, on slow machines.
findings.repro: At Rival with Westshire, Nations screen: pt click 657 218; pt wait 3; pt click 657 218 -> events show 'Not confirmed in time' then 'Click War again...' repeatedly

findings.title: 'Open ground lies about 270 to the north' is not usable: no compass or minimap shows north

findings.title: 'Open ground lies about N to the X' hint changes direction as you follow it
findings.detail: When founding was refused, the hint said '220 to the north' at (131,-84). After walking, it said '250 to the south-east'. At (34,140) it said '180 to the east', then after walking about 112 that way it said '210 to the west'. Each hint is the nearest site from where you stand, so the target jumps around and the distance grows. It took 6 F presses and about 2700 ticks to find a legal site. The last two hints (60 W, then 20 W) were accurate. Expected the hint to stay on one target, or to name a landmark.

findings.title: Breaking a fresh truce with War has no visible cost

The confirm says 'Click War again to break the truce', which is good, but breaking it simply sets relations back to Hostile -60 with no extra penalty, reputation hit or chronicle mention of the broken truce.

findings.title: Chronicle 'Your news' view is flooded with other nations' raids, so nation world events are buried

The HUD chronicle strip labelled 'your news' also lists other nations' stalls. The only nation world event before tick 24000 (tick 19751, 'A bountiful harvest came in across Castleburg...') sat among about 50 raids and 100 relation changes, so a player would never notice that world events are happening to other nations.

findings.title: Drought 'Ration and wait for rain' restlessness penalty is never reported
findings.detail: Option 3 says 'your people grow restless with you'. The result toast and chronicle only say 'Drought struck Hamletton, and you rationed the stores and waited for rain.' There is no number and no visible change; Player Info still reads 'Relationships: 0'. The code lowers every member's relationship with the player, so the free option has a hidden cost the player cannot measure. Expected the result line to state the cost (e.g. 'your 7 members think less of you (-N)') or a visible mood or relationship change.
findings.repro: pt start --seed 108; Start, Begin; create nation (N), found settlement, build a farm (K K); play to tick ~30552 (or pt start --continue from the tick-30003 autosave); click option 3 on the Drought sheet

findings.title: Drought irrigation option takes missing stone from settlement stores without saying so

The other 5 stone came from somewhere unstated (probably the settlement store). Paying from stores is fair, but the option should say where the cost comes from, e.g. 'you 5 + stores 5'. Otherwise the player cannot tell whether an option is affordable.

findings.title: Same shared seed reproduces the starting map but not the world's history (nation names/timing differ)
findings.detail: Share screen shows 'World seed 1450162717' and a ?seed= link. A new world from 1450162717 starts identical to the Ironvale world (same trees/rocks/pawns/chickens at the same distances/bearings, same region and objective; seedworld.png matches world0.png). But history diverges within ~1 game minute: original world tick 850 'Isabella Wood founded the nation of Eastwood', tick 1550 'Peggy Smith ... Bigwood', tick 1702 Ruth Wilson 'Northernville'; same-seed world tick 900 'Isabella Wood founded the nation of Westernham', tick 1400 Ruth Wilson 'Greentown'. Player behaviour differed (walked to a rock in run 1, stood still in run 2), which may explain timing, but the same pawn founding the first nation got a different name. Expected a shared seed to give a friend the same nations, or the Share screen to say only the map is shared.
findings.repro: pt start --seed Ironvale; Start; Begin; play ~1600 ticks; Esc > Share (note seed); Main Menu > Start; clear box, type 1450162717; Begin; pt wait 90; pt events 15

findings.title: Selling in own settlement is coin-starved; Sell Resources sells one unit with no choice
findings.detail: Right after founding, Sell Resources gave 'No merchant here can pay: the richest has 9 coins'. Buying food (25 coins for 1 apple) gave the merchants enough to then buy 1 wood for 20. After that: 'richest has 6 coins', while Market Info showed '4/4 stalls, 40 coins'. I had 437 coins. I could not choose which good or how many to sell. The messages are clear and helpful, but trading is mostly blocked.
findings.repro: Inside new settlement: click Sell Resources (186,445); click Purchase Food (66,445); click Sell Resources again; again

findings.title: Settlement action bar reflows under the pointer, so clicks land on the wrong button
findings.detail: When the market filled, 'Build Stall' disappeared, and a pawn walking up added Order/Talk/Gift rows. Build Farm moved from about (625,445) to (476,445), so my click opened 'Send Caravan (Town era)' instead. Expected: buttons that keep their positions, with unavailable ones disabled rather than removed.
findings.repro: enter own settlement; screenshot; wait for a pawn to approach / market to fill; click where Build Farm was

findings.title: Settlement shows 'Village' tier while the nation's era is still Camp
findings.detail: After building a Farm (tick 8810), the Settlement Info panel said 'Tier: Village (3 buildings)' and the floating label said 'Village of Southernford', but the era panel still said 'Era: Camp (1/4)' with Members 6/10 and Day 1/3 left to do. Two different meanings of 'Village' are on screen at once. It reads as though the goal is already reached when it is not.
findings.repro: seed 102; found a settlement, enter it, press K twice to build a Farm; compare the Settlement Info panel and the era panel

findings.title: Settlement-founding warning about resentful neighbours is overwritten after 8 ticks
findings.detail: 'Settlement founded. Fortressford and Littleford resent a new settlement so near their land.' (tick 5794) is replaced at tick 5802 by 'You are back on your own land. Objective complete...', so the diplomatic consequence is never readable. Also, the large floating settlement label ('0 here, 3/8 residents') draws behind the Chronicle/status HUD and cannot be read.
findings.repro: pt start ... --seed 101; found a settlement within ~260 m of two AI settlements; pt events 10

findings.title: Storehouse/caravan gated behind Town era (Village alone needs Day 3); not reachable in a session, and not shown in era unlocks
findings.detail: 'Send Caravan (Town era)' looks enabled. Clicking it says 'This settlement needs a Storehouse before it can send caravans. The Storehouse is unlocked in the Town era.' The era box lists Village requirements (Village 0/1, Members 6/10, Stalls 2/2, Day 1/3) and Village unlocks (Workshop), but never mentions the Storehouse. With a 10-game-minute day, a caravan is at least 3+ game days away. The button should look disabled, and the era panel should show the path to the Storehouse.
findings.repro: Inside own settlement in Camp era: click Send Caravan (640,445); tap era box (110,58) and scroll

findings.title: Title, main menu and Config screens: white text on light sky-blue, low contrast
findings.detail: Title prompt, menu buttons and Config labels are white/small on ~#72A5E5 with buttons ~#5C9EEB: roughly 2.5:1, under WCAG AA 4.5:1; button edges almost invisible against the background. In-world dark panels are fine by comparison.
findings.repro: pt start --seed 109; pt shot; space; pt shot

findings.title: War confirm status says 'Click War again' but the button now reads 'Confirm'
findings.detail: When armed, the War button is relabelled 'Confirm' while the status line says 'Click War again to declare war on Westshire.' There is no button labelled War on screen at that point.
findings.repro: At Rival with Westshire, click War once and read the button and status line

findings.title: Controls screen page 3 lists debug cheats (F2-F6) to every player
findings.detail: Main menu > Controls page 3/3 shows 'Debug' keys: generate land, spawn pawn, coins, wood, teleport pawns. A new player sees these as normal controls. Expected them hidden in release builds or clearly labelled as developer cheats.
findings.repro: pt start ... ; pt key space; click Controls (480,419); Next twice
alsoTitled: Controls help lists F2-F6 debug cheats and uses touch wording 'Era box (tap)'

findings.title: World-space settlement label draws through full-screen panels and over the HUD
findings.detail: Inside my settlement, the large label '6 here, 7/20 residents' renders through the semi-transparent Nations panel (O) and collides with the Nations/Laws tabs. It also sits behind the pause menu, the Drought sheet and the top-left HUD.
findings.repro: enter own settlement, press O
alsoTitled: Overlay screens (Inventory, Nations/Laws, Pause, Share) draw text with no backing panel over the world and player

findings.title: 'Found elsewhere' hint gives a compass direction, but nothing on screen shows which way is south-east
findings.detail: Pressing F in a claimed area said 'Open ground lies about 170 to the south-east.' The HUD has no compass or heading, so I had to walk and press F again. The second hint said '230 to the north-west' after I had walked about 100 units, which was confusing. After a third try I found a valid spot.
findings.repro: with 50 wood, stand in another nation's land, press f; walk; press f

findings.title: Ctrl+A does not select all in the New World seed box
findings.detail: To paste a shared seed I clicked the seed box ('Ironvale') and pressed Ctrl+A then Backspace; only the last character was deleted, giving 'Ironval1450162717' (seed 1889372902). Needed ~20 Backspaces to clear. The live 'is seed N' preview made the mistake obvious, which is good. (Could partly be key-timing at 2 fps.) A 'Clear' button or select-all on focus would help when pasting a share seed.
findings.repro: Main Menu > Start; click seed box; pt key Control_L+a; pt key BackSpace; pt shot

findings.title: Destructive 'Leave Nation' is the most prominent HUD button
findings.detail: Bright red full-width button directly below the action row; no confirmation observed on hover. Easy misclick for a leader.
findings.repro: n; pt shot

findings.title: First tree's status says '2 apples' but +1 apple shown and Apples = 1
findings.detail: Status 'Gathered 5 wood and 2 apples from tree.' while the float text says '+1 apple' and the inventory shows 1, with energy jumping 83->98 (one apple presumably auto-eaten, unannounced).
findings.repro: pt start ... --seed 101; Begin; walk to nearest tree; pt key e

findings.title: HUD panels briefly drawn off the bottom of the screen right after --continue
findings.detail: First screenshot after `pt start --continue` showed the Inventory, Season and Player Info panels pushed down so they overlap the action buttons and the Player Info energy bar is cut off at the bottom edge. A few seconds later the layout was normal (continued2.png). A fresh New World start did not show this.
findings.repro: Save from pause menu; pt stop; pt start --continue; pt await WORLD; pt shot

findings.title: In-settlement HUD: Inventory panel overlaps action buttons; unexplained Stockpile and price swings
findings.detail: After H then E, the Inventory Info panel sits in the screen centre under the Craft Axe/Craft Pickaxe buttons. 'Collect Stockpile (78)' isn't explained. Stone price fell from 31/28 to 9/8 in about 1300 ticks with no reason given.
findings.repro: pt start ... --seed 101; after founding, go away, pt key h; pt key e

findings.title: Jargon: 'Export replay (USD)', 'border quarrels stop at Rival', 'day 1/2' vs 'Day 1/3'
findings.detail: 'USD' reads as US dollars; 'Rival' is an undefined relation level; Season panel 'day 1/2' (day of season) sits beside Era checklist 'Day 1/3' (days needed) with different meanings. Config Volume says sound only plays in the browser version.
findings.repro: Escape; Share

findings.title: Missing-resource message counts the stockpile without saying so
findings.detail: With 5 stone in inventory, K for a House (15 stone) said 'Need 0 more wood, 5 more stone'. That was only right because 5 stone sat uncollected in the stockpile. Settlement Info 'Next (K)' also changed from Farm to House between visits, while the Build Farm button was still available.
findings.repro: Inside settlement with 21 wood/5 stone and 5 stone in the stockpile: pt key k

findings.title: On entering the settlement, popups overlap and several labels are clipped
findings.detail: On first entering my settlement, two 'Objective complete' popups stacked on top of the chronicle. 'Enter your settlemen' was clipped, the objective panel's 'Gather 20 wood and 5 stone' line was cut off at the bottom of the panel, and a large world-space label '0 here, 1/8 residents' showed through the top HUD.
findings.repro: seed 102; found a settlement (F), then press E to enter

findings.title: Pause menu has no Load entry although controls help lists 'Save, Load, Share, Main Menu'
findings.detail: Pause menu offers Resume, Save, Share, Controls, Main Menu, Quit. Load is only on the main menu. Either add Load or update the help text.
findings.repro: In world: Esc; pt shot

findings.title: Red status toast is clipped: 'No entities within range to interact w'
findings.detail: At 960x540 the red error toast at the top centre cuts off the end of its message.
findings.repro: press e with nothing in reach

findings.title: Settlement floating label is drawn under the top status banner
findings.detail: Standing in Smalltown, the label 'Town of Smalltown / 5 here, 7/12 residents' sits at the top centre exactly where the red status banner appears, so both are partly unreadable.
findings.repro: seed 106; walk into Smalltown (~50,170); press E with nobody in reach

findings.title: Using a rock next to a tree chops the tree instead (interact priority)
findings.detail: Twice `pt walkto rock` + E chopped a nearby tree ('Gathered 8 wood...') rather than mining the rock, because interact prefers tree over rock. This is documented behaviour, but it spends axe durability when the player meant to use the pickaxe. Facing direction could break the tie.
findings.repro: walkto rock near trees (around tick 4291); e

findings.title: Very low frame/tick rate under the shared load; crafting overlay showed a frame late
findings.detail: fps 1-5 and tps 0-17 for most of the session (machine load avg ~54). The first pt start timed out after 60s with an empty game.log; the second worked. Once, state.json said CRAFTING while the screenshot still showed the world view; the overlay appeared ~2s later. Probably the environment, not the game.
findings.repro: pt start under heavy load; key c; pt shot immediately
